rv.q: Stunning performances from Sally Field and Bill Pullman...its power lies in the way it makes a great play as great as it can be: in the finesse and in the details...'
Both performances are masterclasses in moral ambivalence.
Mixing British and American actors in an American play always has risks, and there are moments at the points of high emotion, where Morgan and Coleman’s accents start pitching around a bit.
Field and Pullman both bring a real sense of authenticity to their parts.
Despite its star casting, Herrin's production is disappointingly uneven.
Herrin’s production feels fresh from a factory line, albeit as defective as one of Joe Keller’s cracked cylinders.

cn.t: Sally Field and Bill Pullman lead a restrained revival that savors Miller's complex characters, though critics are divided on whether the staging fully captures the play's dramatic power.
